matched.note: Same defect: removal of Edit/Write permissions.ask entries for ACDSL rule files (**/*.acdsl, acdsl/**) from the global settings template, relying solely on the new acdsl-policy-guard.sh hook + per-repo acdsl/policy.json mode, leaving repos that never adopt gated/strict with no ask-gate.

Same defect: GitRevParse in internal/acdsl/git.go is unused by production code (policyBase/basePolicy use GitMergeBase/GitShowFile) and exercised only by its own test. Golden frames it as a test-only export (code-style/INFO), run frames it as dead code (MAJOR) — same root cause, different severity.

Same underlying defect at the same code block (cmd/hooks/skill-invoke-gate.sh lines 61-73): the post-invocation Bash cat-guard recognizes only a narrow literal shape and is trivially bypassed. Run finding cites the quoting case (line 66 excludes any command containing a quote char, so `cat "path"` is never inspected and never reaches the exact-two-token check); golden GV3-166 catalogs this same guard's fragility via sibling bypass forms (relative Read paths, non-exact-cat command shapes, non-Read/Bash tools).
Identical defect, same file/lines: statusEntry declared before statusCache in internal/server/statuscache.go, violating RULE-GOLANG-FILE-001's alphabetical type-block order (statusCache sorts first).

falsePositives.reason: Claim factually wrong: this diff itself adds internal/routines/routines_test.go:TestHistoryStartedRows, a dedicated multi-row started-supersession unit test with an interleaved started(06:00)/summary(06:30)/started(08:00) sequence that asserts results[0].IsRunning()==true ("run started again") and results[1] is the earlier summary row (Subtype=summary, Result="cells 8/8 ok", SessionId=a) -- exactly the "only the newest survives" contract the finding claims has no dedicated test.

uncataloged.reason: Real, distinct bypass not cataloged as a security defect anywhere in golden: CheckPolicy (internal/acdsl/policy.go:330-335) does `base, isBoundary, baseErr := policyBase(ctx, root, policy); if baseErr != nil { if policy.Mode == PolicyModeFree { return nil, nil } ... }` -- this uses the untrusted working-tree `policy` argument (loaded via LoadPolicy from disk, never reconciled against the base branch via basePolicy() on this path) directly. An agent can set base_ref to a value that fails to resolve (policyBase replaces the entire default candidate chain with the single custom BaseRef per lines 196-199, so GitMergeBase has only one, failing, candidate) together with mode: "free" in the same acdsl/policy.json, and CheckPolicy returns zero diagnostics regardless of what rule/registry changes are made. This is a different mechanism from golden's GV3-001 (working/resolvable base_ref causing a free-mode short-circuit via basePolicy), GV3-002 (base_ref=branch causing isBoundary=false) and GV4-202 (base_ref=HEAD causing vacuous diffs) -- all three require base resolution to SUCCEED; this one requires it to FAIL. The only golden entry touching this exact branch is GV3-108 (INFO/tests: 'CheckPolicy free+unresolvable-base' listed only as an untested edge branch), a materially different claim and root cause (missing test coverage, not an exploitable authorization bypass).

Genuine in-range defect not cataloged: writePolicy (internal/acdsl/dist.go:236-239) does `policy, err := LoadPolicy(root); if err != nil { return "", fmt.Errorf("writePolicy: %w", err) }`, and Dist() (dist.go:106-109) propagates that error as a hard Dist failure. LoadPolicy returns a non-nil error whenever acdsl/policy.json exists but fails to parse (parsePolicy: malformed JSON or unknown mode), so a mid-edit/malformed policy.json on a source repo aborts the entire Dist run with a generic wrapped "writePolicy: ..." error rather than a clearly-attributed policy-parse diagnostic. None of the golden dist.go entries (GV3-034, GV4-204, GV4-211, GV5-238) cover this path.
